reason: Paper seems a useful starting point for gathering the studies at the binding table.
expectation: The paper will be placed at the binding table, ready for a binding step; the next combination is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: Thread and planks might make a binding tool, but preparing the paper seems more directly related to the goal.

effect: The paper is at the binding table, enabling a combination with planks there.
reaction: The placement was straightforward; I’m curious what the planks will make with the paper.
reason: Combine the prepared paper with planks to advance the binding work.
expectation: I expect a support or assembly for the pages, though its exact form is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: Thread and planks may make a binding tool, but the prepared paper now offers a direct next step.

effect: The paper and planks made binding boards with slots for the collected artwork and studies, so I can start fitting them.
reaction: The named slots make the next steps clear.
reason: Add the printed pages to fill the art slot and begin gathering the contents.
expectation: The printed pages will fit into the Art slot of the binding boards.

effect: The printed pages are fitted into the boards; the remaining studies can now be added.
reaction: A straightforward start to assembling the collection.
reason: Add the pressed plant specimen to fill another named slot.
expectation: The specimen will be fitted into the binding boards.

effect: The specimen is fitted, leaving the drawing and four other studies to add.
reaction: The assembly is clear, though the repeated fittings are becoming predictable.
reason: Add the botanical drawing to continue filling the named slots.
expectation: The botanical drawing will fit into the binding boards.

effect: The botanical drawing is fitted, leaving four studies to add.
reason: Add the pond life study to fill another slot.
expectation: The pond life study will fit into the binding boards.

effect: The pond life study is fitted, leaving the rain, wind and star records to add.
reason: Add the rain record to fill another slot.
expectation: The rain record will fit into the binding boards.

effect: The rain record is fitted, leaving the wind record and star chart to add.
reaction: The repeated fittings are still predictable.
reason: Add the wind record to fill another slot.
expectation: The wind record will fit into the binding boards.

effect: The wind record is fitted, leaving the star chart as the last named slot.
reason: Add the star chart using the only offered gameplay action.
expectation: The star chart will fit into the binding boards, completing the collection of named items.

effect: The star chart completed the collection, revealing the goal to bind the encyclopedia.
reaction: Finishing the collection is satisfying, though the fittings were repetitive.
reason: Use thread to bind the collected pages; it is the only offered gameplay action.
expectation: The thread will bind the boards and their contents into an encyclopedia.

effect: The thread bound the collected contents into an encyclopedia, completing the chapter.
reaction: The finished book is a satisfying culmination, though assembling its contents was repetitive.

mostWorthwhile.text: Binding the collected studies into the encyclopedia gave the chapter a clear payoff.

leastWorthwhile.text: Fitting each study individually became predictable and repetitive.

surprise.text: The paper and planks produced binding boards with named slots for all the studies; I had expected some kind of support but wasn't sure what.

arbitrary.text: No action felt clearly purposeless; the individual fittings made sense, even if repeating them felt mechanical.

continue.text: I probably wouldn't continue personally: the final book was satisfying, but the repeated fittings offered few meaningful decisions.
